newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-World oilseeds output seen rising in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-World oilseeds output seen rising in 1997/98.

text.p: Attractive prices and prospects for depleted stocks of soybeans and other oilseeds are expected to push up output for oilseed in 1997/1998, but yield will still be determine by the weather conditions, said Thomas Mielke, editor of the Oil World.

Global oilseed output is forecast to rise to 276.3 million tonnes in 1997/1998 from an estimated 257.3 million tonnes in 1996/1997, he told a palm and laurics oil conference in Kuala Lumpur at the weekend.
"Assuming normal to favourable conditions in most growing areas, we are expecting a boost in world oilseed production by 19 million tonnes in 1997/98," he said.
Mielke said current early prospects for 1997/1998 point to a sharp expansion of oilseed plantings worldwide by 7.6 million hectares to a record 193.3 million hectares.
He added that farmers were already planting larger areas in North America, Europe and elsewhere due to encouraging prices and prospects for depleted stocks.
Mielke said world palm oil output is expected to reach 17.03 million tonnes in 1997.
"While this will set a new record, it will represent a rise of only 0.96 million tonnes or 6 percent," he said.
"This year the expansion is clearly under the lead of Indonesia, where the average mature area will probably be 160,000 hectares or 12.5 percent larger than last year."

Palm oil output in Indonesia, the world's second largest grower, is likely to rise to 5.6 million tonnes in 1997, 6.2 million tonnes in 1998 and to reach 11.7 million tonnes by 2005, Derom Bangun, vice-chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Producers Associations told the conference.
He said planting will increase to 4.6 million hectares in 2005 from 2.26 million currently.
Malaysia, the largest producer of the commodity, produced 8.4 million tonnes in 1996 and output this year is expected at 8.7 million tonnes.

Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik told reporters after opening the conference that the palm oil's share of the global oil and fats industry currently accounts for 35 percent of the overall exports and 16.5 percent of total world consumption.
World copra and palm kernels production is expected to rise to 10.3 million tonnes in 1997, Mielke said.
"This is a record high and up 0.8 million tonnes from last year's relatively low level," he said.
He said the rise was mainly due to a recovery in Philippine copra production and a sizable increase in Indonesian output.
